question: When did Satan enter Judas?
summary: Luke 22:3 places Satan's entering Judas before the Passover, before the Last Supper. John 13:27 places it during the Last Supper itself, immediately after Jesus hands Judas the morsel of bread. The two gospels put the satanic possession on opposite sides of the meal.

reconcile.connective: Adam Clarke resolves the timing by reading two entries of Satan — an earlier one, then a decisive second entry at the supper.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain timing: one gospel places the entry before the meal, the other only after the sop.

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this exact passage directly, resolving the Luke/John timing by reading two distinct entries of Satan into Judas. John Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) was checked (full-text search of the djvu transcript for "Satan", "Judas", and "entered into him") and has no coverage of this specific pairing, so the row's own reconcile-pole author is used instead, per the contract's named alternative.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke's note on John 13:27 directly names two distinct entries of Satan into Judas — one before ('he had entered into him before,' matching Luke 22:3) and a second, confirming entry at the supper — answering the row's timing tension head-on rather than merely describing the verse.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Satan entered into him - He had entered into him before, and now he enters again, to strengthen him in his purpose of delivering up his Master. But the morsel was not the cause of this entering in; the giving of it only marks the time in which the devil confirmed Judas in his traitorous purpose. Some have thought that this morsel was the sacrament of the Lord's Supper: but this is an utter mistake.
That thou doest, do quickly - As if he had said: "Thou art past all counsel; thou hast filled up the measure of thy iniquity, and hast wholly abandoned thyself to Satan; I will not force thee to turn from thy purpose, and without this thou wilt not. Thy designs are all known to me; what thou art determined to do, and I to permit, do directly; delay not, I am ready."
